messages.author: 39f1ac78bd3926ba
messages.subject: No plotdif returned
parts:
Dear all,

I'm running some DIF analyses for a questionnaire of 25 items (with 5 subscales of 5 items each, with a response scale from 1 to 5). I've finished an iterative process with the "scheme=add" command to drop the items showing the greatest -2LL difference, ending up with 3 items that showed no significant difference between the constrained and unconstrained multigroup.

I now want to test if there is really is bias in the 22 items that didn't pass the test by fitting a DIF model on each of the items at a time and examine whether there is a significant change from a constrained multigroup (with anchors) to a model in which I allow either the slope or intercept parameters to vary.

This basically looks as follows (to test DIF for item 1 of the dataset):

puremodel <- 'F1 = 1-5
               F2 = 6-10
               F3 = 11-15
               F4 = 16-20
               F5 = 21-25
               COV = F2*F1 
               COV = F3*F1
               COV = F3*F2
               COV = F4*F1 
               COV = F4*F2 
               COV = F4*F3 
               COV = F5*F1 
               COV = F5*F2 
               COV = F5*F3 
               COV = F5*F4'

anchor <- colnames(data[ ,c(7,14,19)])
mgf <- multipleGroup(data=data, model=puremodel, group=datalanguage, method = "QMCEM", 
                       invariance=c("free_means", "free_varcov", anchor), MAXQUAD=30000, D=5)

dif1a <- DIF(mgf, which.par=c('a1'), scheme='add', return_models=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", 
              items2test=1, p.adjust="FDR", plotdif=TRUE, type="infotrace")

dif1d <- DIF(mgf, which.par=c('d1', 'd2', 'd3', 'd4'), scheme='add', return_models=TRUE, 
              method = "QMCEM", items2test=1, p.adjust="FDR", plotdif=TRUE, type="infotrace")

When I run these models, I get output and no errors (but I do get a warning; see below). However, I don't get the DIF plot. My question is what is the reason that the plot doesn't show?

Many thanks in advance for your ideas!

Best,
Elisabeth

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: No plotdif returned
parts:
This is a multidimensional model at its core, so generally plots supported for unidimensional model comparisons won't be available. The simple structure suggests that you could make plots though by focusing only on the unidimensional subsets though, but this will require some effort on your end to manipulate the returned model objects (which appears to be what you've done in the source code, so that's a start). 

Phil
